newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Ecobank posts higher 1996 profit at $14.9 mln.
newsitem.headline: Ecobank posts higher 1996 profit at $14.9 mln.

text.p: Ecobank Transnational Inc (ETI), a West African banking group, recorded an after tax profit of $14.9 million in 1996, a 20.4 percent increase from 1995, the News Agency of Nigeria reported on Sunday.
Ecobank group chairman Gervais Djondo, who announced this to shareholders at an annual general meeting in Lagos at the weekend, said the 1995 after tax profit was $12.4 million.
According to him, the bank's performance exceeded the target set in its December 1995 action plan.

"The total assets of the group exceeded the $500 million mark for the first time," he said, adding that total deposits also surged, to $372.3 million from $307.6 million in 1995, a growth of 21.1 percent.
Djondo said "1996 was a good year for Ecobank. Our subsidiaries and affiliates performed strongly and profitably."
The objective for 1997 was to substantially expand and increase capital base through retained earnings and new debt and equity capital raising programmes, he said.

The Nigerian unit of the Ecobank group in March raised its capital base to 534 million naira from 133.5 million, surpassing new government requirements that banks operating in Nigeria should have a minimum capitalisation of 500 million naira from 50 million naira previously.
ETI is a private sector financial institution established by authority of the heads of state of the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS).
Owned by 120 individual and institutional shareholders from ECOWAS member countries and with the ECOWAS Fund as the single largest shareholder, Ecobank has branches in six countries.
